title: 1 Robot, No Legs: Meet ISRO's Vyommitra #Shorts
description:
India's next space traveller has no legs, and that's on purpose. Vyommitra, ISRO's half-humanoid robot, is built to simulate astronaut conditions and collect life-support data on Gaganyaan G1. ISRO's crew capsule has already been dropped from a helicopter about 3 to 4 km up to test its parachutes. G1 is the first of three planned uncrewed flights before the crewed flight. It is targeted for Q4 2026 from Sriharikota, with a planned splashdown in the Bay of Bengal. Launch timing is a target and may change.
Subscribe for more hopeful science, one Gaganyaan step at a time.
Sources: ISRO statements as reported in the news. Images: ISRO / PIB (only where licence is confirmed). Footage: stock clips for illustration (Pixabay, NASA), not of the actual event.
#Shorts #Gaganyaan #Vyommitra #ISRO #SpaceIndia

FORMAT: vertical 9:16 YouTube Short, ~45s, English, Indian audience. Series: Gaganyaan Countdown.

SCRIPT:
0:00 Navigator on camera: "India's next space traveller has no legs."
VO: "Meet Vyommitra: ISRO's half-humanoid robot. Head, torso, arms, and no legs. So why send a robot that can't even walk? Because it isn't there to walk. It's built to simulate astronaut conditions and give data on life-support systems. Gaganyaan G1 is targeted for Q4 2026, with no fixed date yet, riding HLVM3, the human-rated LVM3, from Sriharikota. To get here, the capsule was dropped from a helicopter, from 3 to 4 km up, to test its parachutes, after thousands of ground tests. The goals: test the rocket, the orbital module, re-entry and crew module recovery, with a planned splashdown in the Bay of Bengal."
Navigator on camera: "The date has slipped more than once. That's what careful looks like."
VO: "G1 is the first of three planned uncrewed flights before the crewed flight, H1."
Navigator on camera: "It has no legs, but it's paving the way for India's astronauts to fly safely. Follow for every step of Gaganyaan."
